newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Decision on Australian copper smelter pending.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Decision on Australian copper smelter pending.

text.p: Mineral Commodities NL said on Wednesday it could make a final decision by the end of May on whether to seek approvals to build a copper smelter in Queensland, Australia, to service a growing number of copper mines in the region.

Mineral Commodities managing director Peter Topham told Reuters that pending preliminary findings on preferred smelting technologies, a full-blown feasibility study was likely to be started in early March and completed by late May.
"That's really the final stage in the process," Topham said.
A review of the project's estimated capital cost of A$130 million was also under review, he said.
If the project was given the go-ahead, regulatory and environmental agency approvals would be sought, Topham said.
Construction of a smelter with a minimum capacity to process 200,000 tonnes of intermediate concentrate a year would take about two years, Topham said.
The smelter would produce around 55,000 tonnes of contained copper a year, Topham said.
The proposed location of the smelter, the mineral-rich Mount Isa district, had become "like a jig-saw puzzle" as more copper deposits were exploited, he said.
The planned expansion of an existing smelter in Mt Isa by MIM Holdings Ltd to meet internal growth would leave other miners no local outlet for smelting, Topham said.
The only alternative was for the miners to transport concentrates by rail to the port of Townsville, where the material could be shipped by sea to Asia for smelting, he said.
"By developing a copper smelter in the area, we can significantly reduce the costs of transportation," Topham said.
Power for the smelter would be delivered via a new gas pipeline to the region, he said.
Sulphur dioxide generated by the smelter would be transformed into acid and sold to a new phosphate plant being built by WMC Ltd or to neighboring solvent extraction mines, Topham said.

Copper mines in the region include Placer Pacific Ltd's Osborne mine, Australian Resources Ltd's Selwyn mine, Amalg Resources NL's Eloise mine and Topham's own company, with the proposed Trekelano mine.
MIM is developing the Ernest Henry mine in Queensland and plans a new copper mine at Mount Isa. It is increasing smelting capacity to 250,000 tonnes from 175,000 tonnes.
